entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:1
segments:
Who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? that is, as the wise man. 
 
  The boldness of his face shall be changed; his bold air shall be changed to the serenity and dignity of wisdom.  Some render this clause thus: "The strength of his countenance," that is, his firm and assured look, "shall be doubled."

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:2
segments: Obedience to the civil magistrate is a matter not of human expediency, but of divine authority.  We are released from it only when he requires what God forbids.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:3
segments: Be not hasty to go out of his sight; do not hastily withdraw thyself from his service.
To stand before a king, is to serve him,

; hence, to leave his presence, is to quit his service. 
 
  Stand not; be not engaged. 
 
  He doeth whatsoever pleaseth him; and will therefore punish all evil deeds.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:5
segments: Feel no evil thing; or, "know no evil thing;" that is, will not suffer for disobedience.
Time and judgment; the right time and way of doing a thing.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:6
segments: Because to every purpose--great upon him; more literally thus: "For to every puropse there is time and judgment; for the evil of man is great upon him;" that is, time and judgment are necessary to every purpose, because of the evil and uncertainty which belong to human life, and make every good undertaking difficult.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:7
segments: Since it is the plan of God's providence that we should be ignorant of the future, and subject to disappointment in all our undertakings, we ought to unite, with the wise selection of times and means, a spirit of humble dependence upon him and patient submission to his sovereign will.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:8
segments:
Deliver those that are given to it; namely, from death. 
 
The great and the small are alike helpless in the day of death; and ought therefore to be alike humble and diligent in preparing to meet God.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:10
segments: And so I saw the wicked buried; the wicked who had been in power,
, and trusted in their wickedness,

, the Preacher sees buried and forgotten. 
 
  From the place of the holy; probably from Jerusalem, the place of those consecrated to God's service. 
 
  So done,; had been given to wickedness,
, and ruled over men to their own harm,

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:11
segments:
Is not executed speedily; in noticing the final end of the wicked, the Preacher also notices the delay of God's judgment, and its abuse by men. 
 
Nowhere does the desperate wickedness of men show itself more clearly, than in the encouragement which they take from God's gracious forbearance, to harden themselves in iniquity.  Thus they turn to their deeper damnation what he gave them for their salvation.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:14
segments: There is a vanity; though it will in the end be well with the righteous and ill with the wicked, yet, in respect to the course of events in this world, "there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked."

Both are alike subject to "the sufferings of this present time," and to death itself.  The only possible reconciliation of this verse with the two preceding, is the doctrine of a judgment to come.  This the preacher asserts at the close of the book.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:15
segments: Then I commended mirth; see

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 8:17
segments: Cannot find out the work; see the vanity of earthly wisdom is shown from the impossibility of its accomplishing what it undertakes, namely, to comprehend God's ways and works.  See

. 
 
Since God's judgments are unsearchable, and his ways past finding out, true wisdom lies not in endeavoring to comprehend that which is incomprehensible, but in the cheerful resignation of ourselves to his will with a believing, loving, and obedient spirit.
